seo_meta_description: Master Linear Equations on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Interactive Sliders for Unknown Constants
techniques.description: Define equations with variables like 'a' or 'b' instead of numbers. Desmos automatically creates sliders, allowing you to manipulate the graph until it passes through given points.
techniques.when_to_use: When a problem asks for a constant that makes a line pass through specific coordinates.
techniques.pro_tip: Click the slider value to manually type in specific numbers for faster precision.

techniques.title: Regression Formula for Best Fit
techniques.description: Input data points into a table and use the tilde (~) operator to find the slope (m) and y-intercept (b) instantly.
techniques.when_to_use: When given a table of values and asked for the linear equation or a value at a specific x.
techniques.pro_tip: Use the 'plot' button on the table to visualize the points before running the regression.

techniques.title: Intersection Point Analysis
techniques.description: Graph two linear equations and click the intersection point to reveal the (x, y) solution.
techniques.pro_tip: If lines are parallel, Desmos will show no intersection; if they are the same line, it will show an infinite number of points.

techniques.title: Solving for x in Linear Equations
techniques.description: Set the left side of the equation as one line and the right side as another. The x-coordinate of the intersection is your solution.
techniques.when_to_use: Complex linear equations with fractions or parentheses.
techniques.pro_tip: If the lines don't appear, zoom out or click the 'home' icon to reset the view.

techniques.title: Evaluating Functions at Specific Values
techniques.description: Define the function and simply type f(number) in a new line to get the output.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked to find f(x) for a given x.
techniques.pro_tip: Use this to check your work on word problems involving linear growth.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: If $3x + 4y = 12$ and $2x - y = 5$, what is the value of $x + y$?
traditional_method: Step 4: Substitute back to find y

drills.question: Which of the following is the equation of the line that passes through $(2, 5)$ and $(4, 9)$?
drills.desmos_command: Add table with (2,5) and (4,9). Type y1 ~ mx1 + b.
explanation: Step 2: Use regression to find m=2, b=1.

drills.question: What is the x-intercept of the line $4x - 5y = 20$?
explanation: Step 2: Click the x-intercept on the graph.
